disclaimer: Important notes on this reference range table
1. These are BROAD, general adult reference ranges compiled from common published sources
(e.g., Mayo Clinic Labs, ARUP Consult, standard laboratory medicine references).
They are NOT validated against any specific instrument/analyzer or laboratory.
2. Reference ranges are method- and lab-specific. Before clinical or operational use,
replace these with your own laboratory's validated reference ranges.
3. Many entries are qualitative or morphologic findings (e.g., crystals, casts, cell types,
antibody screens, stains) rather than numeric analytes. These are marked with a range
such as "Negative", "None seen", or "Qualitative / not a numeric analyte" in the Notes column.
4. Body-fluid variants (Ascites, CSF, Pleural, Joint Fluid, Stool, "Body Fluid") for chemistry
analytes generally do NOT have fixed population reference ranges — they are interpreted
relative to a paired serum value or clinical context (e.g., SAAG, CSF:serum glucose ratio).
These are marked with an em dash (—) and a note in the Notes column.
5. Hormone/reproductive analytes (FSH, LH, estradiol, progesterone, testosterone, etc.) vary
substantially by age, sex, menstrual cycle phase, and pregnancy status — ranges shown are
6. Therapeutic drug monitoring ranges reflect commonly cited therapeutic (not toxic) windows.
7. Ambiguous or duplicate-looking test name variants (e.g., trailing #, differing capitalization,
spacing) were preserved exactly as provided in the source list to keep a 1:1 row mapping.
